ai.description: This frog reaches 3–4 cm. It is brown with a dark lateral band and a white belly. It features a pointed snout, distinct toe discs, and elongated hind limbs adapted for leaping.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana brachytarsus* is best distinguished by its distinctively short hind limbs, where the tibiotarsal articulation fails to reach the snout when pressed along the body.
ai.habitat: *Indirana brachytarsus* inhabits the leaf litter and rocky stream banks of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Günther's leaping frog is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for small insects and invertebrates among the damp leaf litter and rocky streams of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana brachytarsus* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 100–200 eggs in damp, terrestrial habitats near streams where larvae develop semi-aquatically.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana brachytarsus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Indirana brachytarsus* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, insect-like chirps emitted from moist, rocky habitats near forest streams.
